name: pane
summary: The gt pane: twelve plain-words buttons in a side pane (Claude Code mods, 2.1.290 or later); reorder, rename, add and remove them in plain words

settings.summary: Whether the gt button pane opens when a session starts.
settings.detail:
open    the pane opens by itself at the start of every session  (default)
closed  nothing opens; type /gt-pane-buttons when you want the buttons
off     the pane is never drawn: no pane, no line above the prompt, no buttons

The pane is a column of twelve buttons beside the conversation. Press one (or its key: 1 to 9, 0, q and w)
and it sends its words to Claude as if you had typed them.
The column docks only in Claude Code's fullscreen renderer. In the classic renderer, or in a window
narrower than about 144 columns, the pane cannot sit beside the conversation, so the buttons appear in
a row above the prompt instead. Under the classic renderer a line above them says "pane docks only in
fullscreen — run /tui fullscreen"; run that in the session (Claude Code restarts and resumes it) and
the pane docks.
Your buttons are the list in ~/.claude/golden-thread/pane/buttons.json; change them by asking Claude
("move Overdue to the top"), or press Arrange in the pane
(Update Actions, below it, opens the editor). It needs Claude Code 2.1.290 or later; in an
older Claude Code, or in VS Code, the pane quietly does not appear and nothing else changes.
Change it with /gt:gt-settings or in plain words.

settings.summary: Show your plan allowance at the bottom of the gt pane.
settings.detail:
on   a small line under the buttons: 5-hour 23% · weekly 61% · as of 14:05  (default)
off  nothing is drawn there, and gt does not even open the file the figures come from

The figures are the last ones gt's usage module measured, copied from its saved readings
(~/.claude/golden-thread/usage/latest.json, falling back to readings.jsonl in the same folder). The pane only reads those files; it is read-only here, and
the numbers are never estimated. If there is no reading, nothing is shown. If the newest reading is
older than one hour it is shown dimmed with its age, for example (3h ago), so you can tell it from a fresh one.
The figures refresh when the pane opens or redraws; there is no timer.

settings.summary: How many buttons the gt pane shows (3 to 12).
settings.detail:
12  all twelve buttons  (default)
3-11  only the first N buttons; the rest stay in your list but are not drawn

Why: on a short window the twelve buttons can push Arrange, Update Actions, Open Help and the allowance line off
the bottom of the pane. Showing fewer buttons brings them back into reach. The buttons you hide are not deleted:
they stay in ~/.claude/golden-thread/pane/buttons.json, and Arrange still lists all of them, so you can move a
hidden one up into the visible few. The first N buttons keep their keys (1 to 9, 0, q, w).
Change it with /gt:gt-settings or in plain words ("show only six buttons").
